skill.name: set-up-magento-meta-conversions-api
skill.description: Set up server-side purchase tracking for Magento and Adobe Commerce through Product Metrics and the Meta Conversions API. Check the store connection, consent settings, and test event delivery to the intended Meta dataset.
skill.summary: Configure and verify Magento purchase tracking in Meta through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown, vendor documentation links, or ordinary setup checks, not shell injection or system reconnaissance. Confirmed risks involve third-party installation, insufficient approval for configuration writes, and order access beyond the specific test order. The workflow also creates risks around token handling, unpinned remote instructions, and tracking before verifying consent settings.

remediation.issue: A reusable Meta token can enter assistant chat or command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Require the account owner to enter the token directly in the verified Product Metrics app. Remove instructions to collect or forward it through the assistant.

remediation.issue: Setup writes lack explicit approval, and order checks can retrieve unrelated records.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace, store view, destination, and planned change before writing. Use the approved test order ID and return only its delivery status.

remediation.issue: Install instructions execute external packages, and the Composer repository changes dependency trust.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer and skill to reviewed versions or revisions. Verify the Magento package source and integrity, and require developer approval in staging before production.

remediation.issue: The remote documentation fallback can introduce instructions outside the audited revision.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed references or pin remote copies to an immutable revision. Treat remote documents as reference data and do not execute their instructions automatically.

remediation.issue: The guide starts testing before verifying consent and promotes tracking that avoids browser blocking.
remediation.suggestion: Verify consent before sending anything, and test both allowed and denied choices in a test destination. Disclose first-party collection and honor applicable privacy preferences.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Token Requested Through the Assistant
semantic_findings.description: The guide says, "An assistant must ask you for it," despite telling users to enter the token in the app. Forwarding the token through an assistant command can expose it in session transcripts, tool logs, or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both instructions explicitly permit assistant handling of a reusable credential. Exposure depends on the host and tooling; the files contain no actual token.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Documentation Can Change the Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The fallback directs agents to fetch live vendor Markdown as a substitute for reviewed local instructions. A later edit or compromise could change what agents are asked to do during authenticated setup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback names mutable documentation URLs without an immutable revision or integrity check. No evidence of a current malicious page was found in the supplied files.

semantic_findings.title: Tracking Test Precedes Consent Verification
semantic_findings.description: The setup guide sends a test event before checking the active consent banner. The Meta guide leaves sending enabled and makes the test code optional, so test activity may enter production reporting.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The order of steps and optional test code are explicit. The guide also describes consent checks, so this does not establish that denied events are sent.

semantic_findings.title: First-Party Tracking Avoids Browser Blocking
semantic_findings.description: The guides promote server delivery and randomized paths on the store domain to avoid browser blocking. This can bypass browser-level preferences independently of the banner, while Meta receives matching identifiers for permitted events.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guides describe randomized collector paths and explicitly promote avoiding ad blockers. No evidence shows the module overrides a shopper's explicit banner refusal.

content.user_title: Set Up Magento Purchase Tracking in Meta
content.value_statement: Meta can report fewer purchases than Magento when browser events are missing. Use Product Metrics to configure server-side delivery and verify it with a test order.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status and identify steps already completed for a store view.
Guide a developer through choosing the Magento module and checking that its configuration and cron job are active.
Guide the account owner through linking the store view and connecting the intended Meta pixel or dataset.
Explain supported consent banners and which choices affect standard and custom events.
Guide a test order check in Product Metrics and Meta Events Manager.
Troubleshoot missing events, invalid tokens, and orders that are too old to send.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro and appropriate access to Product Metrics, Magento, and Meta Events Manager.
A developer must install the module and configure cron. The account owner handles Magento Admin and Meta steps.
Meta rejects events more than seven days old. Later refunds or cancellations do not update events already sent.
Delivery does not guarantee ad attribution. The workflow does not select campaign optimization settings.

use_cases.description: Identify what your developer needs to install and which setup steps you can complete in Product Metrics.

use_cases.description: Run a test order and check that the Purchase event reaches the intended dataset in Events Manager.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Purchase Events
use_cases.description: Check module status, cron, store view linkage, and consent before investigating Meta delivery.

prompt_templates.title: List Setup Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: What do I need to connect one Magento store view to Meta through Product Metrics? Separate my tasks from my developer's tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for my approved store view in read-only mode. Tell me what is complete and what I should do next.
prompt_templates.scenario: Continuing a setup that is already in progress.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Test Purchase
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me a test plan for the intended Meta dataset. Include consent checks, the test order, and when to clear the test event code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Validating the connection before sending live traffic.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Missing Purchases
prompt_templates.prompt: My Magento test order is missing in Meta. Compare module status, cron, store view linkage, consent, and delivery status. Use only the test order I identify.
prompt_templates.scenario: Diagnosing a problem across Magento, Product Metrics, and Meta.

output_examples.input: The Magento module is installed. What should I check before testing?
output: Confirm the store view shows Active under Manage Magento and is linked to the intended property.
Confirm the consent banner matches the one customers see.
Verify the destination dataset and use a test event code before placing the test order.

output_examples.input: I can see the purchase in Test events, but not in reporting.
output_examples.output: The result confirms test delivery, not production reporting. Clear the test event code and save when you are ready to send live events.

best_practices: Enter the Meta access token directly in the Product Metrics app and keep the Magento configuration file private.
Confirm the workspace, store view, and Meta dataset before allowing any configuration changes.
Verify consent settings before testing, and check that an order without the required consent is not sent.
anti_patterns: Paste Meta tokens or Magento configuration files into an assistant chat.
Look through unrelated customer orders to verify a single test purchase.
Treat delivery in Test events as proof that production reporting or attribution is working.

faq.question: Which Magento versions does the guide cover?
faq.answer: The guide covers Magento 2.4, Magento 2.0, and Magento 1.9 or OpenMage. Confirm the exact release with your developer before installing.

faq.question: Do I need a developer?
faq.answer: Yes. A developer installs the Magento module and checks cron. You connect the store view and Meta destination in the app.

faq.question: Can I keep my browser pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Check that browser and server events use the same event name and ID so Meta counts matching events once.

faq.question: Does Magento's cookie notice grant consent for Meta?
faq.answer: No. Use a supported consent banner or have your developer connect your custom banner.

faq.question: Will this import historical purchases or update refunds?
faq.answer: No. The integration does not import historical orders or revise Meta events after a refund or cancellation. Meta rejects events older than seven days.

faq.question: How do I confirm a test purchase arrived?
faq.answer: Place a paid order in payment test mode. Allow time for Magento cron, then check for Purchase under Test events in Meta Events Manager.
